metadata.title: Platform Capitalism and the Attention Economy
Platform Capitalism and the Attention Economy

sections.text: Platform capitalism is a new economic form where value is generated by mediating interactions between user groups (a multisided market) and extracting rents from data, attention, and transactions. The attention economy is the revenue mechanism: human attention is scarce, advertisers pay for it, and platforms compete for it by optimizing for engagement above all else.

metadata.title: Platform Capitalism and the Attention Economy

sections.text:
```
+------------------------------------------------------------------+
|            PLATFORM CAPITALISM LANDSCAPE                         |
+------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                                                                  |
|  PLATFORM TYPES (Srnicek)                                        |
|  Advertising: Google, Meta (sell user attention)                 |
|  Cloud: AWS, Azure, GCP (sell computing infrastructure)          |
|  Product: Amazon, Apple App Store (sell products + ecosystem)    |
|  Lean: Uber, Airbnb (asset-light, extract from providers)        |
|  Industrial: Siemens, GE (B2B data extraction)                   |
|                                                                  |
|  SURVEILLANCE CAPITALISM (Zuboff)                                |
|  Behavioral data extraction --> prediction products              |
|  --> behavioral modification --> sold to advertisers             |
|                                                                  |
|  ATTENTION ECONOMY                                               |
|  Herbert Simon: attention is the scarce resource                 |
|  Engagement optimization: maximize time-on-platform             |
|  Outrage, anxiety, and controversy are more engaging            |
|  Variable reward schedules: slot machine dynamics               |
|                                                                  |
|  NETWORK EFFECTS                                                 |
|  Winner-take-all dynamics in platform markets                   |
|  Direct network effects (Facebook: more users = more value)     |
|  Indirect effects (App Store: more apps = more users)           |
+------------------------------------------------------------------+
```
